Subject: Next steps: deployment isolation options & SOC 2 readiness

Hi Susan —

Thanks again for the call this morning — helpful to understand Arbor Health's latency needs and the regulatory constraints around PHI. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we can get security and procurement moving: 

Summary of Redwood options we discussed:
- Private (VPC) deployment in your AWS account with private endpoints and no public ingress — recommended if you want full network control and cloud-managed hardware.
- On‑prem (air‑gapped) appliance: fully isolated, no outbound internet; suitable if your compliance team requires physical separation.
- Dedicated (Redwood-managed) in a private tenant — middle ground for predictable throughput + limited network exposure.

Compliance posture: Redwood completed SOC 2 Type II in June 2025; we also have documented controls for GDPR and offer HIPAA BAAs for customers with covered‑entity requirements. KMS integrations (customer‑managed keys) and audit logs are supported in Private and Dedicated modes.

Immediate requests / asks from our side:
1) Can you share your vendor security questionnaire (or a sample) so we can start filling it out? 
2) If you have a network diagram (CIDR ranges, DMZ, bastion/management VLANs) please attach — helps us size networking approach and airgap feasibility.
3) Are there specific ports/protocols your security team disallows for outbound traffic? Air‑gapped feasibility depends a lot on whether a one‑time provisioning channel is acceptable.
4) Please confirm whether Arbor will require a BAA (HIPAA) for this project.

Proposed next steps:
- Karthik and I will draft a short architecture note (VPC peering vs private endpoint vs air‑gapped) and upload it to the shared folder.
- If helpful, we can loop in a third‑party QSA (Theo Barnes) to help triage questionnaire items and prep for any audit.
- Target: deliver questionnaire response draft + deployment sketch in 3 business days once we have your questionnaire/network sketch.

Attachments: none on this message.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

Susan / Grace —

Following up with a technical sketch and feasibility notes (high level) for the options Grace outlined. I'll upload a formal doc to the shared folder but key points here: 

VPC (customer AWS account) — recommended for fastest time to production:
- Connectivity: Private Endpoint (AWS PrivateLink) into a customer VPC. No public IPs on model hosts.
- Egress: We support routing telemetry and software updates through a customer‑controlled NAT/proxy. You can block all other outbound traffic.
- KMS: Customer‑managed KMS is supported; we can integrate with CloudHSM for key wrapping.
- Audit: Token‑level latency/cost traces and per‑route access logs shipped to your logging S3/CloudWatch.

On‑prem / Air‑gapped — higher compliance margin, more prep work:
- Provisioning model: airgapped appliance delivered to your DC; initial provisioning uses a temporary USB key or an approved one‑time provisioning tunnel under your control. No persistent outbound allowed.
- Ops: We will require an admin management path (bastion or jumpbox) for maintenance windows; this can be physically isolated and scheduled.
- Constraints: Model updates and security patches require an approved transfer mechanism (signed artifacts).

Minimal network requirements (draft):
- Management: SSH (tcp/22) only from a restricted admin jump host (if allowed) OR physical console access for air‑gapped.
- Data plane: internal traffic only (no public-facing ports).
- NTP + internal DNS resolution only; no direct public DNS for hosts in air‑gapped mode.

Attachment: redwood_onprem_airgap_requirements_v1.docx (docx) — contains file integrity checks, signed artifact process, and a checklist for SOC2 mapping. Also attaching a quick PNG sketch for the VPC pattern: deployment_isolation_sketch.png.

Pilot proposition: 2‑week staging pilot in a customer VPC to validate networking/CIDRs and KMS integration before procurement signs off. We'll staff a Red team SE and a solutions engineer.

Happy to jump on a quick call to walk infra through required CIDR ranges and port lists.

Thanks,
Markus Klein
